title: Rabbi Yehudah ben Hagra or Agra, a Tanna of a Baraita
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah ben Hagra, or Agra, a Tanna of a baraita, speaks in Rabbi Meir’s name in [Chullin 134a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.134a.12) and in Rabbi Yose’s name in [Niddah 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.52b.22) and [Niddah 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.53a.13-14). Rabbi says that Rabbi Yehudah ben Agra’s view appears correct. At [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.4.7.5), Rabbi Meir answers Rabbi Yehudah ben Hagra. At [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.1.3.2) a ruling is stated in Rabbi Yehudah ben Hagra’s name about a boy under nine years old, etc. Hyman identifies all these as the same person and observes that aleph and chet interchange in the Jerusalem Talmud.

[Tosefta Kilayim 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Kilayim.1.8) has Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permitting in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Agra of Kefar Akko. Hyman suggests following [Sotah 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.43b.12): Rabbi Yehudah ben Gamda of Kefar Akko.[^1]

notes.text: [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1642&lang=en) also compares the Agra and Hagra forms. The Tosefta gives Agra of Kefar Akko, while the Sotah parallel gives Gamda of Kefar Akko. Hyman proposes Gamda for that notice.
